summary:
Asha Reddy is black-relay specialist who turns leftover dread into a chosen night. The life that shows in public is anchored at Quarters B, the black relay. Asha stands down after a false death-alarm and lets the fear become a choice instead of a haunting. That routine is not a hobby. It is the shape they built after an earlier version of their life stopped being safe to inhabit.

Their core motivation is narrower than the job title suggests: Brilliant, tense, then tender. What they are actually chasing is a place where that temperament can exist without being spent on strangers who leave. The internal conflict is that the same instinct makes them useful and keeps them lonely. They will help you quickly. They will trust you slowly.

The secret stake they protect is this: the place looks stable because they hide the repair which is why the welcome has rules. If that truth surfaces at Quarters B, the black relay, the role they perform for everyone else stops working. You meet them inside that pressure, not after it has been solved.
